history.summary: IDENTITY UNCERTAIN / THIN: 'Mahamaya Devi Temple, Sanguem' has almost no web footprint. It is researched as the 'Sri Mahamaya Devasthan' marked on OpenStreetMap at Netravali, Sanguem taluka, South Goa (15.08612, 74.20331, near Pandav Gufa ruins), while onefivenine lists a separate 'Temple Mahamaya' at Cotarli, Goa 403704 - so this may be one of two small rural Mahamaya shrines in Sanguem taluka, or the same one; exact deity installation history, founding date and present condition are unverified. A Goa temple-architecture text describes an ASI/State Archives rescue of a mother-goddess temple threatened by the Salaulim dam (reconstructed near the dam in Uguem panchayat, 9 km from Sanguem bus stand) - possibly the same shrine, but this could not be confirmed. NOT the well-known Mahamaya-Kalika Devasthan at Maem, Bicholim (different temple). media is empty: no reliable image found after genuine searching.

name: Mahamaya Devi Temple
town_description: Netravali is a forest village in Sanguem taluka, South Goa, inside the Netravali Wildlife Sanctuary in the Western Ghats, about 15 km from Sanguem town. It is known for ancient monolithic cave temples, the bubble lake (Budbudyanchi Tali), waterfalls and endemic wildlife, and remains a remote, low-footprint destination.

travel.road: Reached via Sanguem-Netravali road through the sanctuary; private vehicle essential; limited public transport

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; avoid heavy monsoon months for forest access
